George’s, won the 100 yards, with Stan Botwright and Tom Wiley filling the next two places. With the points scoring 6 down to 1 in each event, we thus got away to a flying start with 9 points from the first race.
This is surely one of the best jumps by an Englishman this season. T.
Tom Wiley (8) was third while among the also rans was—yes, that man’s here again—Percy Wright. In the Shot Putt “that man,” or in other words, P.
His business in the City was twice completely " blitzed " and his son is amongst those missing in the Malava. Those racing included Tom Wiley, Jack Harding, C.
T. Wiley 1st in 100 yards, 220 yards and Long Jump.

Fred Clay ran well in the 100 Yards and also won the Long Jump for the Club, and we were pleased to see Tom Wiley out again. Les Cohen ran a good race in the 2 Miles, and Syd Jarlett and young Dave Main beat Moody, the Police Champion, in the 880 Yards.
In the Long Jump we have had to rely upon Tom Wiley, who a number of times has reached 21 feet. He has been supported by Frank Simmons, Stan Blunden, and our Captain.

In the two jumps we shall feel the pinch most, although Tom Wiley should be good enough to gain us a few first places in the Long Jump. If Frank Simmons only had the opportunity to concentrate on this event he might pull out something good.
Owing to pressure of work, Tom Wiley has not been able to turn out very often in the Long Jump. Owing to injury, Charlie Jones and Frank Simmons have not been able to turn out.
Tom Wiley, who has been unable to compete much this season, showed us that he is still fit by gaining us valuable points in the Field Events, and helping us to win the Relay.
In the Long Jump we have again been unfortunate in not having the services of Tom Wiley, and therefore our Field Events' Captain has been our first string.
Belgrave entries for that meeting included E Gray (100 yds) T D Wiley (100 yds) reserves F W Pritchard and S C Botwright. 440 yds D G Michael, H E Pack, reserves T H Scrimshaw & A A Bird.
